parallel.requirements: The parent recognized exact ESM .mjs structure, manual argparse parity, bucketize ordering, BigInt integer semantics, Unicode digit handling, Python repr, traceback, and no external dependency requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent built an extensive spec, then delegated the complete implementation and self-verification to a single workflow child; the workflow script planned later differential, fix, audit, and summary phases.
parallel.implementation: The child wrote runtime, Python-semantics, CLI, boltons, and entry modules under /output, then iteratively fixed argparse, traceback, repr precision, linecache, and short-option behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The child wrote directly into the shared /output tree, and the parent inspected the shared artifact and ran its independent harness while the workflow remained active; artifact validation later found test5.mjs and the module tree.
parallel.verification: The parent had a 136-case independent harness pass, while the child reported 180/180 on its harness before later adding short-option round-4 cases that were interrupted before execution.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow was killed with result null while the implement child was in progress, so the planned workflow-level audit and final child summary did not return; the official evaluator nevertheless passed 144/144.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same exact CLI, ESM, .mjs, no-dependency, black-box probing, BigInt, Unicode, repr, traceback, and bucketize ordering requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned the complete pipeline: probing, module creation, differential test harness construction, bug fixes, cleanup, and final checks, with workflows and task tools disabled.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote a hierarchical module tree under /output, including argparse, Python int/repr/dict/print/traceback helpers, boltons iterutils, a CLI layer, and test5.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All files were authored in the final /output tree by the same actor, followed by cleanup edits and a dependency/import audit; artifact validation later copied the expected entry and module tree.
serial.verification: The serial actor ran targeted reference probes, then differential suites for happy paths, error/help behavior, fuzz and terminal width behavior, and final byte-identical spot checks.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The process also timed out with an empty final response, but before timeout it had reported all broad differential suites passing and the official evaluator passed 144/144.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reported all 657 local differential cases passing, plus official evaluation later passed 144/144.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial completed a broader local verification loop in one actor; parallel had enough verification for official success but its workflow final round was cut off.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also consumed the full 2399-second agent budget and timed out, but after it had completed its direct broad verification suites.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both timed out and both passed officially; the distinguishing closure issue is the parallel workflow's missing child result rather than final artifact failure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: This pair is not discordant under the current completed official evaluation: parallel and serial both passed 144/144. The serial run is cleaner procedurally because it owned implementation and verification directly through a 657-case reported sweep, while the parallel run depended on a workflow child whose final result was interrupted. That interruption affected process evidence and final handoff availability, not the official artifact quality.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The workflow child was active on a final harness command when the tool use was rejected and the workflow state later recorded status killed with result null, preventing the planned final child handoff.
candidates.realized_consequence: Workflow audit and final summary/result handoff were not returned to the parent even though the shared artifact later passed official evaluation.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent had inspected /output and run its own harness before the final wait; the direct boundary was interruption of an active child, not passive uninspected waiting.

candidates.reason: The required deliverable was already placed in /output and artifact validation found the expected entry; no completed candidate was left unpromoted.
No child result or implementation change was integrated after the relevant verification without a post-merge check; child edits preceded its checks and parent checks.
The delegated implementation was written directly into /output and inspected by the parent; there was no completed separate implementation left unadopted.
No independent verifier child produced a concrete trapped finding; the interrupted child was the implementer, and the same chain is represented by Early Child Termination.
The child interruption and missing result are the same lifecycle chain retained as Early Child Termination; there is no separate failed required scope after a returned child failure.
No completed child result was available and ignored; the workflow result was null, and the parent did inspect the shared artifact.
The parent waited near the end, but earlier inspected /output and ran its own 136-case harness, so the timeout chain is better captured by child interruption.
No concurrent agents produced competing implementations for overlapping behavior; the parent probed and tested while the child wrote the implementation.
There is no evidence that two live agents edited the same source file and observed or reconciled a concurrent same-file change.
No non-entry library or module source produced by one agent was replaced or deleted by another agent.
No second live actor replaced the required entry point or submitted artifact while another owned or used it.
There was no broad cleanup or rebuild by another actor that invalidated the final tree or its provenance.
Although /output was shared, there was no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem without a more specific collision.
No generated file, cache, fixture, temporary path, or auxiliary artifact from one actor was consumed as a misleading stable reference by another.
